defect_observations.observation: Neyman's own switched regions A3(theta1) (eqs. 93-94, journal p. 369, checked on the page image) assign the fiber x1=theta1/2 to the upper section (1-alpha)(theta1-x1)<=x2<=theta1-x1 and use the open bound x2<alpha(theta1-x1) in (94). The handbook instead gives the full fiber 0<x2<=t-x1 at x1=t/2 and closes (94), calling this a 'completion' (lines 12-13, 227-228). It does not record the source's own assignment. It also does not record that, read literally, the source's regions accept no candidate for samples with alpha<=x2/x1<1-alpha when alpha<1/2, which contradicts the source's statement that A3 'may serve as regions of acceptance' (its condition (ii), p. 354). The handbook's annex (line 283, 'including alpha<1/2') shows the repair is deliberate. Not scored as a coverage failure: the entry is complete as written and its boundary change is declared as editorial. One sentence recording the source's (93)-(94) boundary and the reason for the change would close the fidelity gap.

Source eq. (69) (journal p. 362, page image) prints (3/8)delta2 < delta3 < (3/4)delta2 with a strict lower inequality, although its eq. (68) xbar<=L allows equality at x1=x2. Under the title 'The source's length ... comparisons', the handbook states the corrected closed lower bound [3/8,3/4) with the equality case, without noting that this corrects the source. Minor; not scored.

The constant-term part of the completing-the-square identity is asserted, not displayed: 'the remaining constants agree after putting them over tau^2 s^2 (tau^2+s^2)'. The method and denominator are given and the check is mechanical, so it is not scored as a sketch. Displaying the three-line algebra would remove any doubt.

The proof invokes 'The normal transformation theorem' and 'The Neyman--Pearson comparison' by name only, with no cross-reference. Both exist on the reader route: thm:p15-normal-sums (handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex line 314) and thm:p15-neyman-pearson with its complete converse (handbook/parts/p15/hypothesis-tests-and-confidence.tex line 95).
